rows.jp: 「おー、すいとる」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, smell that!"
ghs.assessment: The source remarks that the place is empty or uncrowded, leading into the low guard count. “Smell that” introduces an olfactory action disconnected from the sequence.
ghs.remedy: Use “Oh, it’s empty.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ohhh, smell that!"

rows.jp: 警備員の数が少ない。
rows.en: There were fewer guards than usual.

ghs.en: The number of guards is pretty low.

rows.jp: いつもは十人くらい立ってるのに、今日は二人だ。
rows.en: Normally there would be around ten of them standing about, but today there were only two.

ghs.en: There are always around ten standing around, but today it's only two.
ghs.assessment: The source contrasts the usual ten guards with only two today. “Today it’s only two” uses a singular dummy subject for people.
ghs.remedy: Use “There are usually about ten of them, but today there are only two.”

highlights.text: There are always around ten standing around, but today it's only two.

rows.jp: 暑くなってきて、みんな精神的にも参ってきてるせいか欠席が多い。
rows.en: Maybe because it was getting hotter and everyone was mentally worn down too, a lot of people were absent.

ghs.en: It's gotten hot so, maybe because everybody's mentally cracking up, there's many not attending.
ghs.assessment: The source says many people are absent. “There’s many” has incorrect number agreement and “not attending” lacks a natural object.
ghs.remedy: Use “It’s gotten hot, and perhaps everyone is mentally worn down, because many people are absent.”

highlights.text: It's gotten hot so, maybe because everybody's mentally cracking up, there's many not attending.

rows.jp: だから学食も、どことなく閑散としていた。
rows.en: The cafeteria, too, had an oddly deserted feel.

ghs.en: Therefore, even the cafeteria was in many ways deserted.
ghs.assessment: どことなく means somehow or vaguely. “In many ways” changes it to multiple identifiable respects.
ghs.remedy: Use “As a result, the cafeteria somehow felt deserted too.”

highlights.text: Therefore, even the cafeteria was in many ways deserted.

rows.jp: おかげで競争率高めのメニューにも楽にありつける。
rows.en: On the bright side, even the high-demand meals were easy to get.

ghs.en: Thanks to that, even menus with a high rate of competition can be comfortably obtained.
ghs.assessment: The source refers to highly sought-after menu items. “Menus with a high rate of competition” treats menus as objects acquired and calques the competition expression.
ghs.remedy: Use “Thanks to that, even the most sought-after dishes were easy to get.”

highlights.text: Thanks to that, even menus with a high rate of competition can be comfortably obtained.

rows.jp: いや……とあるコネを使えば、簡単にありつけるのだが。
rows.en: Well... I could always use a certain connection and get one whenever I wanted.

ghs.en: Well... using a certain 'connection', they are always easily obtained.
ghs.assessment: The source says the narrator could obtain one easily by using a certain connection. “They are always obtained” adds habitual frequency and removes his agency.
ghs.remedy: Use “Though I could get one easily by using a certain connection...”

highlights.text: Well... using a certain 'connection', they are always easily obtained.

rows.jp: けどアレは使ってはいけない。
rows.en: But I must never resort to that.

ghs.en: But 'that' is something not to be used.

rows.jp: 禁断の奥義なのだ。

ghs.en: It is forbidden esoterica.
ghs.assessment: The source calls it a forbidden secret technique. Bare “esoterica” names obscure knowledge, not a technique he can deploy.
ghs.remedy: Use “It’s a forbidden secret technique.”

highlights.text: It is forbidden esoterica.

rows.jp: 諸刃の剣だし。

ghs.en: A double-edged sword.

rows.jp: あーでも、遊紗ちゃんかわいいからなぁ。
rows.en: Then again, Yusa was awfully cute.

ghs.en: Ahhh, but Yusa-chan's adorable ain't she.
ghs.assessment: The English uses a tag question without the comma or question mark needed to distinguish it from the statement.
ghs.remedy: Use “Ah, but Yusa-chan is adorable, isn’t she?”

highlights.text: Ahhh, but Yusa-chan's adorable ain't she.

rows.jp: Ｂ定食の食券を買い、カウンターに持っていく。
rows.en: I bought a ticket for Set Meal B and took it to the counter.

ghs.en: I buy a B-meal ticket and bring it to the counter.

rows.jp: 「あらアンタ！　こんなトコで何してんのよ！」（９８ホーン）
rows.en: “Well, look who it is! What’re you doing here?!” (98 phons)

rows.jp: 「どわあああっ！？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "d'WAAAAH?!"

rows.jp: 出た！

ghs.en: She appeared!

rows.jp: 「ご挨拶ね、ぐふふ」

ghs.en: Voice: "Whatta nice hello, guheheh!"

rows.jp: そう言って彼女は、ありふれたファンタジー物に出てくる洞窟奥で酒盛りに興じる異様に巨大な盗賊団のボス（時に入り口より巨躯なケースさえ散見される。ギャグか？）
rows.en: As she spoke, I pictured the freakishly enormous bandit chief carousing deep in the cave of some generic fantasy story. (In some cases, the chief is actually wider than the cave entrance. Is that supposed to be a joke?)

ghs.en: The woman who said this then laughed with a muffled voice in that way typical of those somehow bizarrely giant bandit boss typically encountered merrymaking with alcoholics in the depths of some damp cave in your garden variety fantasy game.

rows.jp: みたいなくぐもった声で笑った。
rows.en: She gave a muffled laugh exactly like his.

rows.jp: 恐かった。

ghs.en: Frightening.

rows.jp: 「驚かさないでよ、おばちゃん。このひ弱な文士をさ」
rows.en: “Don’t scare me like that, ma’am. I’m a delicate man of letters.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't surprise me, madam! I am but a frail man of letters!"

rows.jp: 「アンタが文士ってタマかい。馬鹿も休み休み言いな！」（１１８ホーン）
rows.en: “You? A man of letters? Give me a break!” (118 phons)

rows.jp: ドカン、と怒声が学食に響く。
rows.en: Her roar detonated through the cafeteria.

ghs.en: BOOM!, that's how those harsh words echo throughout the cafeteria.
ghs.assessment: The source says an explosive angry shout reverberates through the cafeteria. “Those harsh words echo” substitutes lexical harshness for the voice’s physical volume.
ghs.remedy: Use “Her angry shout boomed through the cafeteria.”

highlights.text: BOOM!, that's how those harsh words echo throughout the cafeteria.

rows.jp: 強化ガラスがビリビリと震えた（ありえない）。

ghs.en: Tremors rattled the tempered glass windows (improbable).

rows.jp: めっちゃ注目を浴びる俺。
rows.en: Every eye in the room turned to me.

ghs.en: I am bathed in an excess of attention.

rows.jp: 「……声が大きいよ、おばちゃん」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...voice's loud, madam."
ghs.assessment: The source says “Your voice is loud.” The English drops the possessive subject, leaving the fragment “voice’s loud.”
ghs.remedy: Use “Your voice is too loud, ma’am.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...voice's loud, madam."

rows.jp: 「普通に話してるんだけどねぇ。ここの子たちヤワだから！」（９４ホーン）
rows.en: “I’m talking normally! The kids here are just soft!” (94 phons)

rows.jp: 「あんたも手加減してやんなよ！」（１１５ホーン）
rows.en: “You go easy on them too!” (115 phons)

ghs.en: Taichi: "?!"

rows.jp: 危険を察知して、一歩下がる。

ghs.en: Sensing peril, I take a step back.

rows.jp: 巨大な、異形と称していいてのひらが、ゴウッと眼前を横切った。
rows.en: A huge palm—one I could fairly call misshapen—whooshed past my face.

ghs.en: The palm of an hand so gigantic one could correctly call it heteromorphic crossed right before my eyes with a 'whoff'.
ghs.assessment: The article must be “a hand,” and “heteromorphic” is an opaque technical substitute for the source’s description of a grotesquely huge palm.
ghs.remedy: Use “A palm so huge it could be called misshapen whooshed past my face.”

highlights.text: The palm of an hand so gigantic one could correctly call it heteromorphic crossed right before my eyes with a 'whoff'.

rows.jp: 太一（今の）（スキンシップ？）（直撃していたら……）（死！？）
rows.en: Taichi (That just now) (Was that supposed to be friendly?) (If it had hit me...) (Death?!)

ghs.en: Taichi: (That now) (skinship?) (if that had been a direct hit...) (death?!)
ghs.assessment: The first mental fragment means “Just now,” referring to the near blow. “That now” is not an English temporal phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use “(Just now) (Was that skinship?) (If it had hit me...) (Death?!)”

highlights.text: Taichi: (That now) (skinship?) (if that had been a direct hit...) (death?!)

rows.jp: ついつい筒井○隆の七瀬シリーズで使われたみたいな心理表現方法を用いてしまう。
rows.en: I had inadvertently resorted to the kind of psychic prose Yasutaka Tsutsui used in the Nanase series.

ghs.en: All fluky-fluky I made use of a Tsutsui Yasut*ka's Nanase Series-like Process of Intrapsychical Expression.
ghs.assessment: The source says he inadvertently uses a mode of psychological narration like that in the Nanase series. “All fluky-fluky,” the possessive article, and “Process of Intrapsychical Expression” are malformed and distort the claim.
ghs.remedy: Use “Without thinking, I used a style of psychological narration like the one in Tsutsui Yasut*ka’s Nanase series.”

highlights.text: All fluky-fluky I made use of a Tsutsui Yasut*ka's Nanase Series-like Process of Intrapsychical Expression.

rows.jp: なんつうか七瀬繋がりってあると思うし（ねぇよ）。
rows.en: It made sense, what with the Nanase connection. (No, it didn’t.)

ghs.en: For some reason I think there's a connection with Nana-se (seven - currents) (there ain't).
ghs.assessment: The source makes a loose “Nanase connection” joke and immediately denies it. The English invents an explanatory “seven-currents” gloss that is not present.
ghs.remedy: Use “I guess there’s some kind of Nanase connection there. (No there isn’t.)”

highlights.text: For some reason I think there's a connection with Nana-se (seven - currents) (there ain't).

rows.jp: 「やっぱりはしっこいね、アンタは！　ぐふふ」
rows.en: “Quick on your feet as ever, aren’t you! Guhuhu.”

ghs.en: Madam: "Yer really a quick one, ain'tcha! Guheheh!"

rows.jp: 「メシかっくらいにきたんだろ？」

ghs.en: Madam: "So ya came here for some grub or somethin', right?"

rows.jp: 「は、はひ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ye-, YESH."

rows.jp: ライオンに餌をやるような気持ちで、食券を差し出す。
rows.en: Feeling as though I were feeding a lion, I handed her my meal ticket.

ghs.en: With the same feeling as of feeding a hungry lion, I hand over the meal ticket.
ghs.assessment: The source compares his feeling to feeding a lion. “Same feeling as of” is ungrammatical, and “hungry” adds a state not stated.
ghs.remedy: Use “Feeling as though I were feeding a lion, I held out the meal ticket.”

highlights.text: With the same feeling as of feeding a hungry lion, I hand over the meal ticket.

rows.jp: 「遊紗が世話になってるから、サービスしてやるよ」
rows.en: “You’ve been looking after Yusa, so I’ll give you something extra.”

ghs.en: Madam: "Yer always so nice to Yusa, so lemme give ya somethin' good on the house!"

rows.jp: 「ははは、どぉも、ははは」
rows.en: “Ha ha ha... Thanks. Ha ha ha.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "HA-HA-HA, thanks, HA-HA-HA."

rows.jp: そう。

ghs.en: Yes.

rows.jp: この方こそ、究極美少女・遊紗ちゃんの実母であらせられる。
rows.en: This august personage was none other than the mother of Yusa, that peerless young beauty.

ghs.en: It is most assured that this milady here is the very birth mother of 『Ultimate Bishoujo * Yusa-chan』.

rows.jp: つまり彼女も数十年後にはこうな―――
rows.en: Which meant that in a few decades, Yusa too would become—

ghs.en: Therefore, even that girl could, in a number of years, become---

rows.jp: 「どうしたい？　ふらついて」

ghs.en: Yusa's mom: "Wassit now? Ya twitchin'."
ghs.assessment: ふらついて says he is staggering or swaying. “Twitching” describes involuntary small jerks and is the wrong motion.
ghs.remedy: Use “What’s wrong? You’re staggering.”

highlights.text: Yusa's mom: "Wassit now? Ya twitchin'."

rows.jp: 「ソーリー、めまいが」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sooo-rry, bit of vertigo."

rows.jp: 「そりゃいけないね。血肉が足りないんだよ」
rows.en: “That’s no good. You need more meat on your bones.”

ghs.en: Yusa's mom: "Tha'ss no good is it! Ya don't have enough blood in yer meat!"
ghs.assessment: The source jokingly diagnoses a lack of flesh and blood or nourishment. “Blood in your meat” decomposes 血肉 into a nonsensical literal relation.
ghs.remedy: Use “That’s no good. You need more meat on your bones!”

highlights.text: Yusa's mom: "Tha'ss no good is it! Ya don't have enough blood in yer meat!"

rows.jp: 母上様は決めつけた。
rows.en: Her Exalted Motherhood decided this on the spot.

ghs.en: So decided our Most Esteemed Mother.

rows.jp: 「はいよ、Ｓ定食」

ghs.en: Yusa's mom: "Here'ya go, Meal Set S!"

rows.jp: 「Ｓなんてあったんですか」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Does S even exist?"
ghs.assessment: The source asks whether an S set meal existed. “Does S even exist?” drops the meal-set referent and reads as an abstract question about a letter.
ghs.remedy: Use “There was an S set meal?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Does S even exist?"

rows.jp: 「アンタのために作ったのさ！」（１１８ホーン）
rows.en: “I made it just for you!” (118 phons)

rows.jp: 学食中に響き渡る、でかい声で言われた。
rows.en: She announced it loudly enough for the entire cafeteria to hear.

ghs.en: So she said in a voice so gargantuan it resonated throughout the cafeteria.

rows.jp: ヒソヒソ……

ghs.en: Psst, psst...

rows.jp: ヒソヒソされる。

ghs.en: I'm being psst-psst'd about.
ghs.assessment: The source says people are whispering about him. “Psst-psst’d” turns a sound effect into a nonexistent passive verb.
ghs.remedy: Use “People are whispering about me.”

highlights.text: I'm being psst-psst'd about.

rows.jp: 「……ありがたいのですが母上様……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...this one is thankful, Most Esteemed Mother..."

rows.jp: 「あら母上様だなんて嬉しいねぇ！」
rows.en: “Oh, ‘Mother,’ is it? That makes me so happy!”

ghs.en: Yusa's mom: "My, Most Esteemed Mother didja say, that makes me so happy!"

rows.jp: ご飯が倍に盛られた。

ghs.en: The serving of rice doubled.

rows.jp: 「ね、あんた、娘とはどうなのよ？」
rows.en: “So, how are things with my daughter?”

ghs.en: Yusa's Mom: "So, ye, how's it goin' with my daughter?"

rows.jp: 「は、どうと申されますと？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, what could one possibly answer to that?"
ghs.assessment: The source asks what she means by “how are things.” The English instead asks what answer could possibly be given.
ghs.remedy: Use “W-what do you mean, ‘how’?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, what could one possibly answer to that?"

rows.jp: 「うまく手なずけたみたいじゃないか！」
rows.en: “Looks like you’ve got her eating out of your hand!”

ghs.en: Yusa's Mom: "Aint'cha taming her with some skill now!"

rows.jp: 「げふんげふん！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Cough, cough!"

rows.jp: 「婿か。いいねぇ。ぐふふ」
rows.en: “A son-in-law, eh? I like it. Guhuhu.”

ghs.en: Yusa's Mom: "Son-'n-law, eh? Nice innit. Guehehehe!"

rows.jp: 「ムコっ！？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "In law?!?!"
ghs.assessment: 婿 specifically means a groom or son-in-law. “In law” is incomplete and could describe any relation by marriage.
ghs.remedy: Use “S-son-in-law?!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "In law?!?!"

rows.jp: マスヲっ！？

ghs.en: The trout...?!
ghs.assessment: マスヲ invokes the son-in-law character Masuo as a joke. Translating the name as the fish “trout” destroys the cultural and phonetic callback.
ghs.remedy: Use “Masuo?!” and preserve the name-based joke.

highlights.text: The trout...?!

rows.jp: 「あいや、お待ち下され母上様！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Excuse me, but, do please wait, Most Esteemed Mother!"

rows.jp: 「大丈夫さ、心配はいらないよ！」
rows.en: “It’s all right. Nothing to worry about!”

ghs.en: Yusa's mom: "Ye'll do fine, ya don' need worry!"

rows.jp: トンカツが二枚になった。
rows.en: She gave me a second pork cutlet.

ghs.en: The slices of tonkatsu became two.

rows.jp: これは……賄賂！　Ｙ炉ですか？
rows.en: This was... a payoff! A lay-off?

ghs.en: This is... bribery! An offer I can't refuse?!
ghs.assessment: The source follows “bribe” with a compact Y-marked 炉 pun. “An offer I can’t refuse” replaces the wordplay with an unrelated stock phrase.
ghs.remedy: Preserve or annotate the Y-marked pun rather than substituting a different idiom.

highlights.text: This is... bribery! An offer I can't refuse?!

rows.jp: ヒソヒソ……

ghs.en: Psst, psst...

rows.jp: 「あわわわわ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "AhWahWahWahWah!"

rows.jp: 噂されてる！

ghs.en: I'm being rumor'd about!
ghs.assessment: The source says people are gossiping about him. “Rumor’d” is not a standard English passive verb.
ghs.remedy: Use “They’re gossiping about me!”

highlights.text: I'm being rumor'd about!

rows.jp: 俺、今すっごく噂されちゃってる！
rows.en: Everyone was really talking about me now!

ghs.en: I am reeeally being rumor'd about right now!
ghs.assessment: The repeated “rumor’d” remains nonstandard and obscures the escalating realization that others are talking about him.
ghs.remedy: Use “They’re really gossiping about me right now!”

highlights.text: I am reeeally being rumor'd about right now!

rows.jp: 「アンタもいろいろあるんだろうから、難しいこと考えなくてもいいんだよ」
rows.en: “I know you’ve got a lot going on. You don’t need to worry your head over anything complicated.”

ghs.en: Yusa's Mom: "Ye look like ya got a lots of stuff on yer mind, but don'tcha think about all th' hard stuff now!"
ghs.assessment: The quantifier is malformed: English permits “a lot of stuff” or “lots of stuff,” not “a lots of stuff.”
ghs.remedy: Use “You look like you’ve got a lot on your mind...”

highlights.text: Yusa's Mom: "Ye look like ya got a lots of stuff on yer mind, but don'tcha think about all th' hard stuff now!"

rows.jp: 「全部アタシに任しときな」

ghs.en: Yusa's Mom: "Ya leave ever'thing to lil' me!"

rows.jp: 具は薄いワカメしかないはずのみそ汁に、なぜかカニが丸ごとぶち込まれていた。
rows.en: The miso soup was only supposed to contain a few miserable strands of seaweed. Somehow, there was an entire crab stuffed into it.

ghs.en: In that Wakame that one'd expect to always be thin on ingredients, somehow, a crab got tossed in whole.
ghs.assessment: The source says a whole crab has been thrown into miso soup that should contain only thin wakame. The English makes “that Wakame” the container and calls it thin on ingredients.
ghs.remedy: Use “A whole crab had somehow been tossed into the miso soup that should have contained nothing but thin wakame.”

highlights.text: In that Wakame that one'd expect to always be thin on ingredients, somehow, a crab got tossed in whole.

rows.jp: ヒソヒソヒソヒソ……

ghs.en: Psst, psst, psst, psst...
Voice: "...taking bribes..."

ghs.en: Voice: "Crony capitalism..."
ghs.assessment: 天下り refers to officials descending into cushy private-sector posts, not the broader economic system of crony capitalism.
ghs.remedy: Use “Through amakudari...” or “Through bureaucratic golden parachutes...”

highlights.text: Voice: "Crony capitalism..."

rows.jp: 「……インサイダー取引が」

ghs.en: Voice: "Something unlawful going on..."

ghs.en: Voice: "...parties related to the issue of formal visits to the shrine of..."
ghs.assessment: The source identifies someone involved in the shrine-visit controversy. The English trails off after “shrine of,” leaving the object and thought syntactically incomplete.
ghs.remedy: Use “...someone involved in the shrine-visit controversy...”

highlights.text: Voice: "...parties related to the issue of formal visits to the shrine of..."

rows.jp: 「うぐぅ！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Uguu!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "It is way too much!"

ghs.assessment: The source says this amount should be edible because he is a boy. The dialect string “inn’this ’bout how much ya eat” is grammatically incoherent and loses the assertion of capacity.

highlights.text: Yusa's mom: "Hm? Whassat, inn'this 'bout how much ya eat, yer a man after all!"

rows.jp: 自重の倍ほどの重みが、俺を床に押しつけた。
